resources.string: The app will help you find the best places in the city: cafes, restaurants, parks, museums, and entertainment for children.
All recommendations are based on reviews from locals and tourists.
The cultural capital of Russia, known for its museums, parks, architecture, and drawbridges.
Here you will find the best places in St. Petersburg: cozy cafes, delicious restaurants, picturesque parks, interesting museums, and entertainment for children.
• Tap ☰ in the top left corner to open the menu
• Select a category to see a list of places
• Tap on a place to see details

The Hobz bakery and confectionery, opened by a hereditary baker from Tunisia, attracts with the aroma of fresh baguettes and Viennese pastries. The small café with its clever twist is a must-visit after a walk through the Russian or Ethnographic Museums, located just a few minutes away. In addition to great pastries, the café has an impressive menu of appetizers and hot dishes, and authentic French, English, and Turkish breakfasts are served all day from 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

The legendary "Sever-Metropol" café has been operating since 1903. In 2025, the café completely renovated its interior: the walls are decorated with bas-reliefs featuring its signature white bears, and comfortable sofas have appeared. The signature "Sever" or "Lunnoye" pastries are a true taste of childhood for St. Petersburg residents. Here you can not only have coffee with dessert but also enjoy a full meal — for example, a chicken Kiev or pancakes with sour cream.

"Forgot Sugar" is a café serving desserts and candies according to original recipes, all of which are sugar-free. The cafés distinguishing feature is a huge hovering cloud between the first and second floors. A cozy atmosphere, tall potted plants zone the space.

FermA at the entrance to "Passage" from Nevsky Prospekt set the trend for custard buns with delicate fillings. The cafés display always features several types, and we also recommend paying attention to the waffle tubes and chocolate cherry cake. You can sit with coffee and desserts near the buildings main staircase or in a small quiet room, away from the noise and shopping.

The Leningrad Zoo is one of the oldest zoos in Russia, founded in 1865. It is home to over 600 species of animals, birds, and reptiles. Children can see polar bears, tigers, monkeys, and participate in interactive feeding sessions.

The Georgian restaurant "Eli Shumeli" is located in the very center of St. Petersburg, at 20 Nevsky Prospekt. The hall is located in a semi-basement — a very colorful and atmospheric place. The service is top-notch, the waiters are polite and attentive. Georgian cuisine will delight lovers of khinkali, khachapuri, and other dishes. The location is very convenient for tourists.
The wine club "Loza" is located at 150 Nevsky Prospekt. A cozy establishment with a good wine list. Metro stations and convenient access roads are nearby.

The Japanese cuisine restaurant "WASABI" is located at 54/3 Nevsky Prospekt, near the "Nevsky Prospekt" and "Gostiny Dvor" metro stations. The café is constantly changing and modernizing. Poetry evenings for students, graduation parties for schoolchildren, and business meetings are held here.

D^Or is located on the second floor of the shopping gallery adjacent to "Passage" and has been well known to luxury shopping enthusiasts for over 20 years. The menu offers a variety of dishes: escalope of foie gras with berries, pike cutlets, octopus appetizer. Over 15 signature desserts are offered, and the editorial choice is tiramisu with a rich coffee and dark chocolate flavor, panna cotta with fresh berries, and cherry-coconut parfait.

The Summer Garden is the oldest park in St. Petersburg, founded by order of Peter I. Here you will see marble sculptures, fountains, and the Summer Palace — the emperors first residence, now a museum. The garden is very quiet and peaceful, especially in the mornings. A great place to relax in the city center.

Catherine Park is a landscape park around the Catherine Palace in Tsarskoye Selo (Pushkin town). Its territory includes ponds, pavilions, grottoes, and bridges. The park combines regular French planning and picturesque English landscapes. The best time for a walk is a sunny day when the gold of the foliage reflects in the water.

Alexander Garden near the Admiralty walls is one of the oldest parks in the city, laid out in 1872. Here you can see a fountain, flower beds, and an oak tree planted by Emperor Alexander II himself. The garden is a popular recreation spot for city residents and visitors to the capital.

Mikhailovsky Garden is a landscape garden adjacent to the Russian Museum. It features beautiful alleys, fountains, marble sculptures, and a pond. The garden is a perfect place for a quiet walk in the very center of the city, away from the noise of Nevsky Prospekt.

The State Hermitage Museum is one of the largest art museums in the world, located in a complex of buildings along the Palace Embankment. The Hermitage includes the Winter Palace, the Small, Old, and New Hermitages, as well as the Hermitage Theatre. The museums collection covers art from antiquity to the 20th century, including masterpieces by Leonardo da Vinci, Rembrandt, and Matisse. Be sure to visit: the Raphael Loggias, the "Peacock" clock, and the St. George Hall.

The Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography named after Peter the Great (Kunstkamera) is Russias oldest museum, founded by Peter I. It is known for its anatomical collection of Peter Is freaks and an exhibition dedicated to the culture of the worlds peoples. This is not only an exhibition of human anomalies but also a deep look into the history of science. Here you can see ethnographic collections, the Gottorp Globe Planetarium, and a shamans flute made from a femur.

The State Russian Museum is the main museum of Russian fine art with an extensive collection — from icons to avant-garde. The main building is the Mikhailovsky Palace, but there are other branches: the Mikhailovsky Castle, the Stroganov and Marble Palaces. The collection includes icons, paintings by Bryullov, Repin, Aivazovsky, and Vasnetsov. Over 400,000 exhibits.

The Faberge Museum is located in the Shuvalov Palace on the Fontanka River. The museum houses the worlds largest collection of works by Carl Faberge, including the legendary imperial Easter eggs. Visitors can also see decorative arts, paintings, and jewelry.

Planetarium No. 1 is the largest planetarium in the world with a dome diameter of 37 meters. Full-dome shows, astronomy lectures, telescope observations. Children will find it very interesting! Interactive programs for schoolchildren are regularly held.

The Oceanarium is one of the largest oceanariums in Europe. A tunnel with sharks, stingrays, penguins, tropical fish. Shark and penguin feeding shows. More than 5,000 inhabitants from around the world. Interactive zones and touch tanks.

The Peter and Paul Fortress is the symbol of the founding of St. Petersburg and the historical heart of the city on Hare Island. Here you can climb the cathedral bell tower, enter the Trubetskoy Bastion prison, and walk along the fortress walls. Every day at noon, a cannon shot is fired from here. A great place for a walk with a view of the Neva and the Palace Embankment.
St. Petersburg is a city of art, history, and romance. The cultural capital of Russia, known for its museums, parks, architecture, and drawbridges. It is a city that never ceases to amaze.
🏛️ Over 200 museums, including the world-famous Hermitage
🌉 About 800 bridges, of which 22 are drawbridges
✨ Included in the UNESCO World Heritage List
🌙 Famous White Nights from late May to mid-July
🎭 The birthplace of Russian ballet — the Mariinsky Theatre
